name: American Legion Post 32 Mess Hall Restaurant

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The facility’s heat sanitizing dish machine was unable to reach 160F after multiple runs of the dish machine (between 152-157F).  Utilize the triple sink (wash-rinse-sanitize) until the dish machine has been repaired. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/23- due to the facility’s hours. Notify the inspector before then if the machine has been serviced. Dish machines that sanitize food contact surfaces by heat must reach a minimum of 160F.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee wash hands, then fail to use a barrier to shut off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was conducted. Ensure hand washing ends with the use of a barrier to shut off the faucet after drying hands to prevent recontaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 6 cans (4 tomato paste and 2 green beans) with large dents along the seams. CORRECTED- discussed with the person in charge (PIC). Items were removed from service to be returned to their supplier for credit. Ensure all hermetically sealed cans are inspected upon arrival. Large dents along the body and any dents along the seams may act as a point of entry and harborage for Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ground beef stored above pollock in the outdoor 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- the ground beef was moved above the chicken. Ensure all foods in coolers are stored to reflect proper storage order (ready to eat foods on top, followed by increasing cooking temperatures) to prevent cross contamination. Inspector provided an educational handout to share with employees.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the baffles of the ice machine. CORRECTED- the PIC wiped the baffles with a sanitizer cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple methods of food contact sanitation failing to meet sanitizing requirements:
1) The chemical sanitizing quaternary ammonia at the bar triple sink was below the required concentration. CORRECTED- an extra sanitizer tablet was added, and 200 ppm quaternary ammonia was observed.
2) The kitchen’s heat sanitizing dish machine took 3 runs to meet proper heat sanitizing temperatures (160F and above). 
Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to ensure proper sanitizing concentration (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia) and temperatures (160F and above).
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a difference of 6F between the facility’s heat plate and their own. Discussed replacing the battery. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/16 to verify that the facility’s temperature sanitizing dish plate is able to accurately measure the surface temperature of dishes.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.12 Temperature Measuring Devices, Ambient Air and Water. (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be designed to be easily readable and accurate to ±1.5°C in the intended range of use. (B) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Two of the three employees present during today’s inspection do not have Food Handler Certificates. The inspector provided a handout of ANSI-Approved courses to the PIC. Ensure all employees who do any degree of food handling (including bar tending and waiting tables) complete Food Handler training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was an empty sanitizer bucket observed to be in the handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The inspectors removed the bucket and discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use and that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- The soda gun nozzle and holder were observed to have slight soil residue accumulation on them. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned the nozzle and holder during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There was not a sanitizer bucket made and available in the kitchen. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at a proper concentration of 400ppm. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made and available for use in the kitchen during all hours of food preparation and cooking.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The floor under the dish machine is observed to be in need of cleaning. There was a dead roach, along with an accumulation of food debris and soil residue, under the dish machine. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed several cockroaches in the kitchen. Cockroaches were concentrated under the triple sink. Both adults and nymphs were observed. Pest control has greatly reduced the number of cockroaches, but small populations still persist. Alternative pest control methods may be needed to eradicate the pests completely.

There is a hole in the wall behind the triple sink that needs to be sealed as well. Inspectors recommend using spray foam to seal the hole. Once spray foam is used, shave foam flush with the wall and paint it to make it smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. 

Ensure door sweeps allow no light to pass under the door.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed three areas to have soiled food-contact surfaces. 

The first two areas were the bar soda nozzles. Discussed with PIC at bar. Ensure that soda nozzles are taken apart and cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. 

The third area was the ice machine baffle. The front of the baffle was clean except for the edges near where it attaches to the ice bin. These edges are holding soils. Discussed with PIC at bar. Ensure that the baffle is cleaned thoroughly enough to remove soils from all parts of the baffle. 

Inspector will return 09/15/2025 to re-inspect these food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a bottle of juice and two containers of coffee creamer to not be date marked at the bar. Discussed with bar PIC. Ensure that all items labeled “refrigerate after opening” are date marked within 24 hours of opening and kept for no longer than 7 days. Inspector will return 09/15/2025 to re-inspect date marking practices.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector noticed two areas that cockroaches could be entering the facility. 

The first area is the event room door to the outdoor seating area. There is a gap under this door that must be sealed to prevent pest entry.

The second area is the bar door to the outdoor seating area. There is a gap under this door as well that could allow pests in the building.

Ensure these gaps are sealed to prevent pest entry, this is especially important given the pest presence in the kitchen.

Inspector will return 9/15/2025 to ensure gaps have been sealed.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cockroaches in the kitchen. Both adults and nymphs were observed. 5-10 were seen free roaming in the kitchen and a large amount were seen on sticky traps. Facility is keeping up with cleaning, the only area in the kitchen that could use more cleaning is behind the dish machine. All other areas were observed to be clean. There are also no gaps or holes observed in the kitchen where cockroaches could be getting in. All food is being stored protected in plastic containers or cold-holding units. Inspector will return 9/15/2025 to re-inspect pest presence. Ensure that pest control comes and pest presence is reduced before this visit.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The bar freezer containing just pizzas was observed to have a build-up of ice. Ice is not considered smooth, nonabsorbent, or corrosion resistant. Discussed with PIC. Ensure freezer is defrosted regularly enough to keep it free of ice.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the bar cooler being used to chill glasses to contain debris. The bottom of the unit is lined with wire mesh, and underneath is dirty. Discussed with bar PIC. Ensure this area is cleaned regularly enough to keep it free of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed two instances of date marking violations in the facility.

The first instance was at the bar, where the inspector observed the juice containers to not bear date marks. Discussed with the PIC, and they had date marks added to the containers. Ensure that containers are date marked within 24 hours of opening to preserve food safety. Violation is corrected on site.

The second instance was in the kitchen. Inspector observed 3 containers full of sauce cups to be past the 7-day maximum that date marked food can be kept. Discussed dates with PIC, and PIC immediately threw out the sauces and replaced them with fresh.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple live roaches of different life stages in the kitchen. Roaches were crawling on walls and piping, mainly concentrated near the dish machine. PIC has been previously educated on pest control, and informed inspector that pest management has been here every week or two since the inspection in July. Ensure pest management continues to come. It would not be a bad idea to remove all equipment from the kitchen for a deep clean of both the room and the equipment.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Pre-made to-go cups of sour cream and a container of green beans were observed with no date marking.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded the green beans and labeled the sour cream.  The sour cream is used up and refilled every Friday.  Ensure all containers are date marked and discarded after 7 days.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Multiple cockroaches and a mouse were observed during today’s inspection.  PIC stated their pest control company is aware of the problem and has been coming out every 2 weeks to treat.  She also stated they had changed distributors for fish, and then switched back to their original distributor to see if the roaches become lower in numbers.  Ensure pest control is coming out every 2 weeks to eradicate all pests and rodents.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The back double door cooler had an ambient temperature of 46F.  After using a probe thermometer, several items were 44F or under, and were moved to the clear door cooler in the kitchen.  Some items (milk, eggs) were 46F or over and were discarded.  PIC contacted the contractor to schedule a time to service the cooler.  Do not use the cooler for items that have to be refrigerated until the cooler is serviced and properly working. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two containers were in the back cooler with no date mark.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded the items.  Ensure all containers are date marked and discarded after 7 days.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Some clean pans and lids were observed to contain food splatter.  Discussed with PIC, who pulled all the soiled items.  Ensure clean dishes are protected from food splatter by storing them inverted or covered.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The coffee machine was observed to contain an accumulation of residue.  Discussed with PIC, who corrected on-site.  Ensure the coffee machine is cleaned regularly.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The clear door cooler in the kitchen is not keeping a temperature of 41F or less on the bottom shelves. Discussed with PIC. The cool air comes from the top of the unit and blows throughout the cooler, but if the shelves are overstocked, the cold air cannot properly cool the bottom.  Ensure the bottom shelves are only for shelf stable food items and the top shelves are not overstocked.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two containers were improperly date marked and corrected on site.  Discussed with PIC, when food it moved from its original container, it must be properly date marked.  Ensure all food containers are properly date marked.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Multiple holes were observed by the hand sink, the 3 part sink, and the dish machine.  Holes in the walls are not easily cleanable and can also aid in pest entry.  Ensure holes are sealed or caulked.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Baffles were observed to contain dust and grease debris.  Sticker present on the hood shows Robert Meacham cleaned the hood and baffles on 01/17/2023 and comes to the facility every 4 months.  Baffles are to be cleaned in between scheduled hood cleaning service to prevent dust and grease build-up.  Ensure baffles are cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of food.

(REPEAT)Fan observed in kitchen to contain dust.  Non food contact surfaces shall be free of dust to prevent contamination of food and clean food contact surfaces.  Ensure fan is cleaned regularly to prevent dust build-up.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Temperature measuring device not ordered for dish machine.  Discussed with employees and PIC regarding the importance of obtaining a temperature measuring device.  Provided PIC with information on how to obtain this device.  Ensure device is obtained and available to regularly measure dish machine temperature.  Will follow-up in 7 days.

4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink in kitchen was not supplied with paper towels upon arrival, PIC restocked paper towels immediately.  Paper towels shall be supplied at all hand washing sinks.  Ensure paper towels are supplied at all times.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink contained shrimp upon arrival.  PIC immediately removed shrimp when informed.  Hand washing sink is only to be used for hand washing.  Ensure hand washing sink is not used for any other purpose than hand washing.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometers were not observed in any food coolers.  Thermometers shall to have the measure of air temperature visible at all times in case of cooler failure.  Ensure thermometers are placed in all food coolers.

Facility does not have temperature measuring device for dish machine.  Discussed with PIC about purchasing a temperature disk or temperature sensitive stickers to measure the temperature of the dish machine for sanitation.  Digital read on dish machine may not always be accurate.  Ensure temperature measuring device is present and dish machine is regularly checked.

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Clean cups were observed to be stacked on top of one another while still wet.  Dishes shall be dried or stored in a position to air dry before stacking to prevent mold growth and contamination.  Ensure dishes and cups are dry before stacking.

Pan lids were observed to contain dust and food debris under prep table.  Store food contact surfaces in a manner to prevent contamination from splash or dust accumulation.  Ensure lids are covered or stored in a clean safe area.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Baffles were observed to contain dust and grease debris.  Sticker present on the hood shows Robert Meacham cleaned the hood and baffles on 8/9/22 and comes to the facility every 4 months.  Baffles are to be cleaned in between scheduled hood cleaning service to prevent dust and grease build-up.  Ensure baffles are cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of food.

Fan observed in kitchen to contain dust.  Non food contact surfaces shall be free of dust to prevent contamination of food and clean food contact surfaces.  Ensure fan is cleaned regularly to prevent dust build-up.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11  (C) Ice is not protected from contamination at the bar. See attached photo. Soda lines are hooked up inside the ice bin behind the bar. Ice in this case is considered a food product and cannot be in contact with equipment that is potentially harboring pathogens and not regularly cleaned. 

Inspector called AA during inspection. Per AA facility may elect to either 1) to divide the bin into two separate compartments, left and right, with ice on the right side only. Each compartment must be individually watertight so either compartment is not at risk of contamination from the other 2) Keep a smaller bin or container within the compartment itself for ice. That bin must be watertight itself and must be routinely cleaned OR 3) Cease use of bin for ice altogether and keep only items such as well mixers and bottles. 

Inspector advised PIC Mandy to figure out which option works best for them and to call/email picture of the chosen solution by the date listed to the right. If no contact has been made by 3/2, inspector will re-inspect at the expense of permit holder.
